## *The Divine Soul.*

According to Proclus <note>Proclus (412–485 AD) was a Greek Neoplatonist philosopher who systematized the philosophy of Plato into a complex metaphysical hierarchy.</note> in his *Theology of Plato*, divine beings are categorized in four ways: **by union**, **by participation**, **by contact**, and **by likeness**. <note>original Greek: "καθ’ ἕνωσιν, κατὰ μέθεξιν, κατὰ συναφὴν, καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν."</note> That is, through union, through communion, through contact or conjunction, and through similitude. The Platonists <note>Refers to the Neoplatonic school, which viewed the universe as a series of "emanations" descending from a single, perfect source called "the One."</note> teach that intellectual beings are divine **through union**, because they are joined most closely to simple unity—that is, to God. Those souls are called divine **through communion** (or participation) which they simply term "divine"; these are joined to the One by a tighter bond of kinship than other souls, namely by being made sharers in the essence of the Mind. <term>Mind: In this philosophical context, "Mind" (or *Nous*) is the first level of reality below "the One," representing pure intellect and the realm of divine ideas.</term> **Through contact**, "Demonic" souls <note>Daimonic souls: The word "demonic" here refers to *daimones*, which in Greek philosophy were intermediary spirits or guardian geniuses that bridged the gap between gods and mortals; they were not considered "evil" as in later traditions.</note> are considered divine because they receive the Mind through their actions; the Platonists call these the "constant followers of the gods," and attribute to them "right opinion." <note>Right opinion: A state of knowledge that is factually true but lacks the deep, rational understanding of *why* it is true, which is reserved for the higher Mind.</note> Finally, human souls are called divine **through likeness**, insofar as they are led back to God as their principle or origin; for through...

...from likeness, the returns to the principles of all things occur. <note>original Greek: "ὁμοιότητος αἱ πρὸς τὰς ἀρχὰς ἐπιστροφαί." This refers to the Neoplatonic concept that a thing returns to its source by becoming like it.</note> Through this likeness, the returns of all things to their own principles are accomplished; these are the souls which, because they do not receive the perfect mind, the Platonists sometimes call only "followers of the gods," and they attribute to them an uncertain or wavering opinion. <note>The author is describing a class of souls that lack direct intellectual "vision" of the divine and instead rely on "opinion," which in Platonic thought is a lower form of knowledge that can be true or false.</note>

## *They are not deprived of all choice.*

For virtue, says Plato in the tenth book of the *Republic*, is free and knows no master; according to how much one either honors or neglects it, so will he possess more or less of it. The blame belongs to the one who chooses; God is beyond all blame. <note>original: "Virtus... libera, seruire nescia." This is a reference to the famous line from the Myth of Er (*Republic* 617e): "Virtue is without a master... the blame is his who chooses: God is blameless."</note> Indeed, Plotinus says in the *Enneads* (Book 3, Chapter 2, Section 9): Providence ought not to be so all-encompassing that we ourselves are nothing. If Providence were everything and existed alone, it would no longer be Providence. <note>Plotinus argues that for divine "Providence" to exist, there must be independent beings for it to care for; if humans had no free will, we would merely be extensions of the divine rather than subjects of its care.</note> For this reason, Plato rightly teaches in the *Protagoras* that God distributed **shame** and **justice** to all human beings. He offers an elegant fable: **Jupiter**, he says, fearing for our race lest it perish entirely, sent **Mercury** to bring shame and justice to men. These were to be the ornaments and bonds of cities, and the guardians of holy friendship among citizens, and con-

But Mercury asked Jupiter in what manner he should give shame <note>original: "pudorem," translating the Greek "aidōs," which implies a sense of moral shame, modesty, or respect for others.</note> and justice to men: "And should I," he said, "distribute these in the same way that the other arts have been distributed? Should I, therefore, Father, place shame and justice among men in this way, or shall I distribute them universally to all?" "To all," said Jupiter; "Let all be participants in them: otherwise, cities would not exist at all, if only a few were partakers of them as they are with the other arts."

# ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH

### *Angels who do not have absolute freedom of choice.*

Angels understand their own operations, says Maimonides in *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: "More Neuochim," the seminal work by the 12th-century Jewish philosopher Moses Maimonides that sought to reconcile Aristotelian philosophy with Hebrew Bible theology.</note>, part 2, chapter 7; they possess the faculty of choosing and governing. However, they do not possess that same liberty and power of governance which we humans have, which is concerned entirely with created things. The divine Law <note>original: "Lex diuina," usually referring to the Holy Scriptures or the Torah.</note> teaches us this: for this reason, the Angel said to Lot in Genesis 19, verse 22: "I shall not be able to do anything, until you arrive there." <note>The angel's statement to Lot implies that his power is constrained by a divine mandate or specific conditions, unlike the broader, more unpredictable freedom of human choice.</note>

## There is a mystery of seven degrees, etc.

In the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work in the literature of Jewish mystical thought known as Kabbalah.</note>, section *In the Beginning* <note>original: *In principio*; this refers to the section of the Zohar commenting on the first book of the Torah, *Bereshit* (Genesis).</note>, column 60: Seven Sephirot <note>The ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> are attributed to the life of man, who is made in the image of God. (These are the seven steps by which the work of creation was completed.) 

The first is the degree of Mercy <note>original: *misericordiæ*, referring to the Sephirah *Chesed*.</note>; the second of Power <note>original: *potentiæ*, referring to *Gevurah*.</note>; the third of Beauty <note>original: *decoris*, referring to *Tiferet*.</note>; the fourth of Victory <note>original: *victoriæ*, referring to *Netzach*.</note>; the fifth of Majesty <note>original: *maiestatis*, referring to *Hod*.</note>; the sixth of Foundation <note>original: *fundamenti*, referring to *Yesod*.</note>; the seventh of Kingdom <note>original: *regni*, referring to *Malkuth*.</note>, or of Justice, the end of days. 

Man begins his life in the degree of mercy; his days are completed in the degree of Justice, which is called the end of days. Ten years are assigned to each degree. Therefore, since there are seven degrees, a man can live seventy years. This is what is said in Psalm 89, verse 10 <note>Psalm 89:10 in the Vulgate numbering, which is Psalm 90:10 in modern English and Hebrew Bibles.</note>: *The days of our years in themselves are seventy years.* It continues.

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic belief that the human lifespan of seventy years is derived from the seven lower Sephirot, with each divine attribute governing a ten-year period of life.</summary>

# *And to transmute into another body.*

The Jews believe that souls change bodies, or are revolved from one body into another; the *Pythagoreans* <note>Followers of the ancient Greek philosopher Pythagoras, who was famous for teaching the immortality and migration of the soul.</note> call this <term>Metempsychosis: a Greek term meaning "the passage of the soul from one body to another."</term>. Of this, Rabbi Yehiel <note>likely Yehiel ben Joseph of Paris or a similar authority cited in Kabbalistic works</note> identifies two species in the book *The Temple of the Lord* <note>original Latin: *Templum Domini*; likely referring to a Hebrew work such as *Heikhal HaKodesh*</note>. One of these he calls <term>Gilgul: a Hebrew word meaning "rolling" or "cycle," referring to the standard process of reincarnation from birth.</term> (revolution); the other <term>Ibbur: literally "impregnation," a mystical concept where a righteous soul temporarily joins a living person to help them fulfill a commandment.</term>, that is, "impregnation."

He defines *Revolution* <note>Hebrew: *Gilgul*</note> as that by which someone "returns and reverts to the days of youth" <note>original Hebrew: *chazar ve-shav el yemey ha-ne'urim*</note> and returns to the days of infancy, so that those matters for which he could not make amends in <term>Gehenna: in Jewish tradition, a place of spiritual purification for the soul after death.</term>, he may perfectly complete by being born again.

1. If he has not properly observed some necessary commandment, or has omitted it entirely, they hold that he must be reborn so that he may fulfill that task, or something similar; a capacity for action which he could not attain in Gehenna. Then God restores to him those good works which he had performed in the previous period—works which had been useless to him at that time because of the sins he had committed.

->### on the thirtieth chapter.<-

He shall complete his garment through the commandments which he performed in the first body, and by right he shall wear them, for "the wicked may prepare, but the righteous shall wear it." <note>original Hebrew: ישלים לבושו במצות שפעל בגוף הראשון ובדין ילבש אותם ויכין רשע וצדיק ילבש. This refers to the idea that the "garment" of the soul—its spiritual form in the afterlife—is woven from the good deeds performed during its earthly life.</note>

That is: He shall perfect his garment in the commandments which he performed in his former body: and then he shall put them on, just as it is written in Job 27:17: *the wicked may prepare it, but the righteous is clothed in them.*

2. Since all souls are created as male and female; if either of the two, whether male or female, has turned out wicked, or has departed from the body without children; they say for this reason that <term>revolution: the process of reincarnation (Gilgul).</term> is necessary, so that through cycles of this kind, the souls may exist together as pious, male and female, and likewise as fruitful <note>This reflects the Kabbalistic belief that souls are originally joined as male-female pairs and must eventually reunite in a state of purity and fulfillment of the commandment to multiply.</note>.

3. So that in this way the stain of original sin <note>The author uses the Christian term "original sin" to describe the primordial flaw or "tarnishing" of the soul that requires purification through multiple lifetimes.</note> may be washed away.

Furthermore, this order is maintained so that, having considered the merit of the souls, they are reborn from righteous or unrighteous parents until the third revolution, according to that passage in Job 33:29: *Behold, God works all these things three times with each person.* Sometimes it is for a thousand years, according to that passage in Psalm 105:8 <note>The Latin text cites Psalm 104, following the Vulgate numbering, which corresponds to Psalm 105 in modern English Bibles.</note>: *Which He commanded to a thousand generations.* They are revolved, however, not only into [human] bodies—

### And to transmute into another body.

The Jews believe that souls change bodies, or are cycled from bodies into bodies; the Pythagoreans call this *metempsychosis* <note>original Greek: μετεμψύχωσιν, referring to the transmigration of the soul into a new body</note>. Rabbi Iechiel identifies two species of this in the book *The Temple of the Lord* <note>original Latin: *Templum Domini*. This likely refers to the Hebrew work *Beit HaShem* or *Heikhal HaShem*</note>. One of these he calls *revolution* <note>Hebrew: גלגול, *Gilgul*</note>: the other *impregnation* <note>Hebrew: עיבור, *Ibbur*</note>.

He defines *Revolution* <note>Gilgul</note> as that by which someone "returns and reverts to the days of youth" <note>original Hebrew: חוזר ושב אל ימי הנעורים</note>, so that he might perfectly complete, by being born again, those things for which he could not make satisfaction in Gehenna <note>a place of spiritual purification or reckoning in the afterlife</note>.

1. If he has not rightly observed some necessary commandment, or has omitted it entirely, they hold that he is reborn so that he may fulfill that, or something similar; for he could not achieve such a virtue of action in Gehenna. Then God restores to him those good works which he had performed in the previous period, in which they had been useless to him on account of the sins committed;

# Regarding the thirtieth chapter.

He will complete his garment through the commandments which he performed in his first body, and by right he shall wear them; as it is said, "the wicked prepares and the righteous shall wear them." <note>original Hebrew: ישלים לבושו במצות שפעל בגוף הראשון ובדין ילבש אותם ויכין רשע וצדיק ילבש. In Kabbalistic thought, the "garment" of the soul in the afterlife is woven from the good deeds and commandments (mitzvot) performed during one's physical life.</note>

*That is*: He will perfect his garment in the commandments, which he performed in his previous body: and then he will put them on, just as it is written in *Job 27:17*: "The wicked man prepared, but the righteous man is clothed in them."

2. Since all souls are created as male and female <note>This refers to the mystical belief that every soul is originally an androgynous being that is split into male and female halves before birth</note>; if either one, whether male or female, has turned out wicked, or has departed from the body without children; they therefore say that a *revolution* <term>revolution: Latin *revolutio*, translating the Hebrew *Gilgul*, the cycling of a soul through different bodies</term> is necessary. This is so that through these kinds of cycles, the souls may eventually exist together as pious, as male and female, and likewise as fruitful <note>fulfilling the essential commandment to "be fruitful and multiply"</note>.

3. So that in this way the stain of original sin may be washed away.
This order is maintained so that, having considered the merit of the souls, they are reborn from righteous or unrighteous parents for up to three revolutions, according to that verse in *Job 33:29*: "Behold, God works all these things three times for each person." At other times, this occurs over a thousand years, according to *Psalm 104:8*: "Which he commanded to a thousand generations." <note>In many modern English Bibles, this is numbered as Psalm 105:8.</note>

Indeed, they are revolved <note>reincarnated</note> not only into human bodies—

When the man falls into sin, it departs from him and rebukes him; but when he is worthy, it clings to him, and he is perfected through his good deeds.

While she appears "empty" or dark to us on Earth, she is "full" of light to a being positioned above her in the celestial spheres.</note>

Furthermore, he says in Book 1, Chapter 2 of the third *Ennead* <note>original: Enn. 3. lib. 1. cap. 2.</note>: "What is the cause that, when the same conditions occur—such as when the Moon appears—one person should turn to robbery while another does not at all? And when similar influences come from the surrounding heavens or the air, why should one person fall ill while another does not? Indeed, even from the same labors, why does this man turn out wealthy while that one remains poor?"

Therefore, the aspects of the Moon or any other star are not the causes of those things that happen to men; but, as he says in the second *Ennead*, Book 3, Chapter 14 <note>original: Enn. 2. lib. 3. cap. 14.</note>: "If indeed someone has cast away riches, he himself is the cause; if they are stolen, the thief is the cause; if a loss occurs by shipwreck, the many factors that converged gave cause to the damage."

Glory, however, is held either justly or unjustly: if justly, it was acquired both through one's duties and the fairness of those judging; if unjustly, it **proceeds** <note>The catchword at the bottom of the page "profi-" refers to the Latin word *proficiscitur*, which is translated here as "proceeds."</note> from the injustice of those bestowing the honor.

## The newborn is clothed in that disposition
## which is appropriate to the time.

For this reason, as Plato rightly teaches, as soon as an infant begins to understand what is being said, the nurse, the mother, the tutor <term>pædagogus: in antiquity, a domestic educator or guardian who supervised a child's conduct and early learning</term>, and the father himself all strive competitively in this matter, so that the boy might turn out best in every action and word. They teach him, of course, and press upon him through the demonstration of examples that one thing is just, another unjust; this is beautiful <note>or "noble," from the Greek *kalon*</note>, that is shameful; one is pious, another impious; what must be done, and what must not. 

If the boy obeys willingly, they think the matter is going excellently; but if not, they straighten him with threats and blows, just like a warped and crooked piece of wood. <note>original: "ὁ νῦν δή λόγος ἡμῖν ὁμολογηθεὶς μενέτω , ὡς οἵ γε ὀρθῶς πεπαιδευμένοι, σχεδὸν ἀγαθοὶ γίγνονται."</note> "Let the argument we have just agreed upon stand: that those who have been rightly educated generally become good men." Therefore, let it be established between us by common consensus regarding the matter itself, that those who have been cultivated through proper discipline almost always turn out to be good men.

...just as a wise man loves the body and nourishes it as long as the soul is assisted by it; so too, when the soul is hindered by the body, being affected by weariness, it should chastise the body with love, driven by a more fervent spirit. The *Platonists* <note>Followers of Plato whose philosophy deeply influenced Renaissance thought, particularly the idea that the soul mediates between the material and spiritual worlds.</note> elegantly demonstrate that this is suited to human nature.

They say that since it is characteristic of all divine minds to gaze upon higher things and to provide for lower things, it is also characteristic of our own soul, which cares for and cultivates not only its own body, but also the bodies of all earthly things and the earth itself. But the more burdensome this providence <note>original: *providentia*. Here referring to the soul's duty to care for the physical world.</note> is—because it must care for things that are more fragile and less fit to maintain order—the more the soul is distracted from contemplating higher things. 

Yet, it is not entirely distracted: for through the intellect we seek all truth; through the will we love all good; and through our actions <note>original: *operationes*</note> we worship God, who is indeed all that is truly good. These three duties of moral integrity <note>term: *honestatis officia*. A concept derived from Cicero, referring to the moral obligations that constitute a virtuous life.</note> signify that even in so great a storm of this world’s sea, the soul always looks up to heavenly things; and by looking up at them, it is daily seized by a more fervent love for them. Some of the wise men who lived after the Amoraim <note>The Amoraim were the Jewish scholars of the 3rd to 5th centuries whose discussions comprise the Gemara, the second part of the Talmud.</note> were called Gaonim <note>original Hebrew: קצת החכמים שהיו אחרי האמוראים נקראו גאונים</note>.

Certain of the wise men who succeeded the Amoraim are called Gaonim. I have heard that they were so named because they were exceptionally well-versed in the Talmud, in which there are sixty tractates. For "Gaon" <note>original Hebrew: גאון</note> equals sixty when calculated by Gematria <term>Gematria</term> <note>A traditional Jewish system of assigning numerical values to letters. The letters of Gaon—Gimel (3), Aleph (1), Vav (6), and Nun (50)—sum to 60, matching the 60 volumes of the Talmud.</note>.

## *But if a cloud should lie upon the earth, etc.*

To understand this matter, it must be known from the Talmud that the Hebrews were accustomed to determine the beginning of their months based on the physical sighting of the New Moon. If the Moon did not appear on the thirtieth day, then the thirtieth day was considered the final day of the preceding month (for a Hebrew month never consists of more than thirty days). However, if the Moon was sighted on the thirtieth day, that thirtieth day became the first day of the new month. But if the appearance of the Moon could not be observed because of clouds, a state of doubt arose as to whether the thirtieth day was the end of the previous month or the beginning of the next. For this reason, if the sighting of the Moon was obscured by clouds...

# CONCLUSIONS
## *fifty Kabbalistic*
### *explained in the notes.*

### I.
Father and mother, son and daughter fulfill the mystery of the holy name and the Sephirot <note>The Sephirot are the ten creative powers or attributes in Jewish mysticism through which the Infinite is revealed.</note>.

### II.
The Monad <term>Monad: derived from the Greek word for "unit," representing the singular, indivisible origin of all things</term>, taken simply, is the hidden one above, the good pleasure of God, the crown: the principal essence, the "paternal depth" according to the Platonists. The Monad multiplied within itself, or begotten from the Monad, is the infinite word, wisdom, and Father: the Platonists call this the "first light," while Philo <note>Philo of Alexandria (c. 20 BCE – 50 CE), a Hellenistic Jewish philosopher who sought to harmonize the Torah with Greek philosophy</note> calls it the image of God and the son of God.

The Son, or the written law, after the promises...

### Kabbalistic Conclusions

Abraham and Isaac, in the time of Jacob—to whom the key of the heavens was handed over—were like the rising sun. Later, in the age of Joseph, it <note>Referring to the divine light or wisdom discussed in the previous sections</note> existed as the sun approaching closer to us. Afterward, through the ministry of Moses and Aaron, when it was distinctly set before the people, it was like the sun shining at noon. Finally, during the reigns of David and Solomon, it was diffused into the oral law, just as the sun illuminates the Moon. From this, understand what is meant by "peace to him who is far off, and to him who is near" <note>A reference to Isaiah 57:19, interpreted here as the reach of divine emanation</note>. This is the mystery of the Sephirot <term>Sephirot: the ten creative powers or attributes of God in Kabbalah, often envisioned as a tree or a sequence of lights</term>.

### XIV.

The light of the garment and the light of snow are nothing other than celestial and terrestrial matter <note>In Kabbalistic thought, the "garment" often refers to the *Tallit* or the primordial light with which God clothed Himself to create the universe. ### XV.

Seven lights were created before the world: the light of the Law <note>original: *lux legis*; referring to the Torah</note>, the light of repentance, the light of the Garden of Eden, the light of Gehenna <note>original: *lux gehennæ*; the place of purification or spiritual punishment</note>, the light of the throne of glory, the light of the holy house <note>the Temple in Jerusalem</note>, and the light of the name of the Messiah.

Sixty myriads <note>A "myriad" is 10,000; thus, 600,000 souls. This number corresponds to the traditional count of the Israelites present at Mount Sinai, representing the totality of the Jewish people.</note> of souls were created at the beginning.

### XVII.

The events that occurred at the birth of Venus concerning Poros and Penia <note>original: *Poro, & Peniæ*; a reference to Plato's *Symposium*, where Love (Eros) is conceived by Resource (Poros) and Poverty (Penia). ### XVIII.

The garment of souls reveals their distinction <note>This suggests that the "ethereal body" or spiritual covering of a soul reflects its individual nature, merit, or rank.</note>.

Souls descend toward generation like a star; they descend through Cancer and ascend through Capricorn <note>A common concept in Neoplatonic and Hermetic astrology, popularized by Porphyry and Macrobius, which posits that souls enter the physical world through the "Gate of Men" (Cancer) and return to the divine through the "Gate of the Gods" (Capricorn).</note>.

[...the rest] of souls fall into the star and the triangle <note>This fragment likely concludes a previous point about the geometric or astrological placement of souls as they descend into the material world.</note>.

### XXI.
There are degrees of the soul: emanation, creation, formation, and making; [these are] <term>Nephesh</term>, <term>Ruach</term>, and <term>Neshamah</term> <note>These three terms represent the traditional Kabbalistic hierarchy of the soul: *Nephesh* is the vital/animal soul associated with the physical body; *Ruach* is the spirit or emotional soul; and *Neshamah* is the highest intellectual soul that connects the human to the Divine. Pico aligns these with the four neo-Platonic levels of reality: Emanation, Creation, Formation, and Action.</note>.

### XXII.
The soul of emanation and creation is the soul of Wisdom and Understanding <note>original: *Sapientiæ, & Intelligentiæ*; referring to the Sefirot *Chokhmah* and *Binah*</note>; hence [we speak of] sons and servants <note>In Kabbalistic thought, "sons" are those who serve God out of love and intellectual understanding (the higher souls), while "servants" are those who serve out of fear or duty (the lower souls).</note>.

### XXIII.
The Mind is divine through union; divine souls [are divine] through communion; Demonic souls through contact; and Human souls through likeness <note>Pico here outlines a hierarchy of spiritual participation. The "Mind" achieves total unity with God, while humans only possess a "likeness" or image of the divine.</note>.

### XXIV.
Souls, according to their different states through the triad of reversion, life, and essence, are placed under Pluto, Neptune, and Jupiter <note>Pico is synthesizing Greek mythology with theology. In this context, Pluto often represents the earth or the descent into matter, Neptune the intermediate realm of change or flow, and Jupiter the celestial or governing intellect.</note>.

### XXV.
The intellect is material, attained, and abstract <note>original: *materialis, adeptus, & abſtractus*. This reflects the Aristotelian classification of the mind: the "material" (potential) intellect, the "attained" (active) intellect through learning, and the "abstract" intellect which exists independently of matter.</note>.

### XXVI.
<term>Grace</term> <note>original Hebrew: *Chen* (חן). While it literally means "Grace," it is also a traditional Kabbalistic acronym for *Chochmah Nisteret* or "Hidden Wisdom."</note>, the lower hill, is divided into the bundle of the living and the Garden of Eden below...

# Fifty Conclusions

->Kabbalistic<-

<column-break/>

### XLII.
Samaël <note>original: *Semaël*; in Kabbalah, Samael is often the angel of death or an accuser, representing the "left side" or severity.</note> is the cause of death and impurity, and Metatron <note>original: *Mitatron*; a high celestial being and scribe of heaven, often identified as the "Prince of the Countenance."</note> is the cause of life and purity; similarly, he rejoices with the Almighty name <note>The Latin text is fragmented here due to the binding, but likely refers to Metatron sharing a name with the Almighty, as his name is numerically equivalent to *Shaddai*.</note>.

### XLIII.
The "legs of the bridegroom" <note>A symbolic reference to the lower emanations or the physical manifestation of divine presence.</note> signify the time of the Messiah's arrival among the Jews.

### XLIV.
Because the Messiah [son] of David <note>original: *Messias Dauid*; the final, triumphant redeemer in Jewish tradition.</note> will come from the hills according to the Jews, he will not die like the Messiah ben Joseph <note>Messiah ben Joseph is a figure in Jewish eschatology who precedes the Davidic Messiah and is destined to fall in battle against the enemies of Israel.</note>, who will be killed and will remain dead for some time, because he will come forth only from a lower hill.

### XLV.
Because it is written that the bride is unwilling to defile her feet once they have been washed <note>A reference to Song of Solomon 5:3: "I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?"</note>, they [the Jews] therefore deny that the Messiah [son] of David will come before the solitude of the seventh millennium <note>original: *7 millenarii*; referring to the "Sabbath of the World," a thousand-year period of rest or the Messianic Age following 6,000 years of history.</note>.

### XLVI.
Since the Messiah—whether coming from among the living or from the dead—is called David, <margin>Zohar <note>The *Zohar* (Radiance) is the foundational work of Jewish mystical thought, or Kabbalah.</note></margin> the Jews seem to admit two Messiahs in vain. <note>Pico is arguing here that the distinction between the suffering Messiah (ben Joseph) and the kingly Messiah (ben David) is unnecessary if both are seen as manifestations of the same Davidic force.</note>

<meta>This page continues Giovanni Pico della Mirandola’s "Kabbalistic Conclusions," specifically continuing the series of numbered aphorisms. While the previous page discussed the nature of the soul, the two Messiahs (son of David and son of Joseph), and the symbolic "feet" of the divine, this page moves toward the relationship between the Jewish people and the Divine Presence (Shekhinah), the mechanics of resurrection, and the religious obligations of women.</meta>

# Kabbalistic Conclusions

<header>Kabbalistic [Conclusions]</header>

->XLVII.<-

The Congregation of Israel <note>original: *Congregatio Israël*; in Kabbalah, this refers to the *Shekhinah*, the feminine aspect of the Divine that dwells among the people.</note> and the Oral Law are called "the Kingdom" <note>original: *Regnum*; refers to *Malkuth*, the tenth and final emanation (*Sefirah*) on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, which represents the physical world and the Divine Presence on earth.</note> by the Jews, and they also call it the "Matron" <note>original: *Matrona*; a title for the Shekhinah.</note>, whom they say has long been separated from the King; just as kings have ceased to exist among them. It is therefore clear, according to their own logic, that the scepter has departed from the house of Judah; therefore, the time for the arrival of the Messiah has already passed. <note>Pico is using a traditional Christian polemic here, arguing that if the Jews no longer have an earthly kingdom or a "King," then according to biblical prophecy (Genesis 49:10), the Messiah must have already come—implying Jesus Christ.</note>

->XLVIII.<-

The mystery of the oil of Obadiah’s wife <note>A reference to the miracle in 2 Kings 4:1–7, where a small jar of oil multiplied to save a widow from debt.</note> reveals the mystery of the *luz* bone: <term>Luz: In Jewish folklore and Kabbalah, an indestructible bone (often identified as the coccyx or a bone in the skull) from which the body will be miraculously reconstructed during the resurrection of the dead.</term> Furthermore, he who understands how God first introduced man into the world shall also understand which people are to be the first to be resurrected.

->XLIX.<-

The worlds are divided into a unity and a triad. <note>This likely refers to the division of the four Kabbalistic worlds: *Atziluth* (the world of emanation/unity) and the triad of *Beriah* (creation), *Yetzirah* (formation), and *Assiah* (action).</note>

->L.<-

Three things are proposed for women to observe: Fire, blood, and the dough-offering. <note>These are the *Mitzvot* (commandments) traditionally specific to women: *Hadlat HaNer* (lighting the Sabbath candles, or "fire"), *Niddah* (laws of family purity regarding "blood"), and *Challah* (separating a portion of "dough" for the priest).</note>

<summary>In these conclusions, Pico della Mirandola argues that Jewish tradition inadvertently proves the Messiah has already arrived and explores the mystical mechanics of resurrection and the ritual duties of women.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Malkuth, Messiah, luz bone, resurrection, Obadiah, women's mitzvot, Jewish-Christian polemics</keywords>

<meta>This page transitions from the end of the subject index (Page 669) to the front matter of the book, specifically the Royal Privilege. ## Extract from the Royal
## Privilege.

<note>A decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring intricate foliate and scrollwork designs is used for the opening word 'BY' (originally 'PAR'). Such initials were common in 17th-century printing to signal the start of a formal legal document.</note>

BY the Grace and Privilege of the King, Toussaint du Bray, Sworn Merchant Bookseller in Paris, is permitted to print or have printed, sell, and distribute a book entitled *A Kabbalistic Disputation on the Soul by Rabbi Israel, and a Rhythmic Work by Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra on the methods by which the Hebrews are accustomed to interpret the Law, with added commentaries from the Zohar and other Rabbinic books, together with those points that agree with the doctrine of Plato*, <note>original: "Disputatio Cabalistica de Anima R. Israël & opus Rhythmicum. R. Praise be to God, Master of the worlds: Dweller of the high heavens and the heights of the atmospheres, whose essence is without end <note>original: "Ein Sof," referring to God's infinite, unknowable aspect before manifestation</note>, beyond matter and form, beyond both speech and thought: The Unique God, the Eternal, who preceded the primordial matter <term>Hyle|A philosophical term for the basic, undifferentiated "stuff" or first matter of the universe</term>: All things were found by Him—the many heavens, the highest heavens, and the vast multitudes of His myriads of angels <note>original: "Erelim" and "Ofanim," two distinct classes of angelic beings in Jewish liturgy and mysticism</note>. From the very beginning of His making, He said, "Let there be light," and there was a blazing light. He brought forth from the hiddenness of His word and created from that light the element of fire and the air, and He created the spirit of the sea and the dry land to be an inheritance for all creatures. From the brilliance of His glory, He created the stars, the constellations, and the heavens, which possess specific measure and distances. He is the one who mounts the spheres and the stars upon them for their rotations; He is the one who sustains the circular movements and the spherical heavens, and He placed within them those awesome bodies as lights. Their Creator made them constant servants to delight in the telling of His glory without the need for speech or sight, as they maintain their positions in their celestial systems.

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical unity between the Creator, the Torah, and humanity. Regarding this level, thus it is written: "He tells His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel" (Psalm 147:19). These are two distinct levels: Jacob and Israel—one is revealed and the other is hidden. What does this refer to? Rather, anyone who is circumcised and marked with the Holy Name is given those matters revealed in the Torah <note>original: *Oraita*</note>; that is to say, they make known to him at first the letters and the beginnings of the chapters. Thus it is written: "He tells His words to Jacob"—this is well said. But "His statutes and His judgments to Israel"—these refer to the mysteries of the Torah, the laws of the Torah, and the secrets of the Torah, which must not be revealed except to one who is at a higher level, as is fitting. And this is to demonstrate what we have said: that the existence of the world depends on the three aforementioned things <note>The Holy One, the Torah, and Israel</note>; and "The Righteous One is the foundation of the world" (Proverbs 10:25)—he is the one who sustains it so it does not falter, so long as he listens to the voice of the Lord and His Torah. Therefore, our Sages of blessed memory said <note>original: *ARZAL*, an acronym for 'Adoneinu Rabbeinu Zichronam Livracha'</note>: "At the hour when his time arrives to go out into the open air of the world, they administer an oath to him <note>The soul of the newborn</note> that he should occupy himself with the Torah and the commandments," since all the work of Creation and the purpose of the Beginning is for the sake of Man, that he might strive in the Torah. As we say in the Zohar, in the portion of *Terumah*: "Once the world was created, every single thing..."

## what reason should the Chosen People have any subjugation or inclination

And after having prefaced what was necessary according to our premise, it is proper to address a profound doubt that occupies us. One feels a certain trepidation in expressing with the "tongue of the pen" <note>original: *kulmos*</note> that which resides in the heart of the seeker. Yet, through the pen of a "ready scribe," the matter shall be expanded, bringing forth those theoretical concepts formed in the soul more effectively than could be told by mouth or tongue. 

This is because we have established the premise that man is a **righteous one who rules in the fear of God** and that **he sustains the world** <note>original: *ihu mekayem alma*</note> as previously mentioned. Because of this, a doubt arises which every person of understanding must consider, whether they approach it through the Written Torah or the Oral Tradition. From these sources comes a doubt and confusion that someone of my limited intellect cannot easily weigh or balance. 

For a person gropes within himself like a blind man in the dark, fearing to inquire or investigate too deeply, lest "a fire break out and catch in thorns" (Exodus 22:5), and the "scab" of doubt spreads—a "leprosy" of heresy <term>Minut: specifically referring to sectarianism or views that deviate from established religious law</term> and apostasy <term>Hitpakerut: a term for total abandonment of religious restraint or faith</term>. In the midst of this struggle, one falls into the state described by Job:

> I am blameless; I do not know myself; I loathe my life. (Job 9:21)

When the time comes for her to descend into the world, she dwells in the Garden of Eden for thirty days to behold the glory of the Master of the righteous, then ascends to her celestial place. Afterward, she descends to the physical world. The King adorns her with seven crowns until she arrives and enters within the body of a human being. ## This is the Torah which the Lord commanded to speak.

-> 7 <-

-> It speaks of those words that a person strived for, even though they were unable <-
-> to understand them in their essence; they will all be rectified in him <-
-> at the time of the Resurrection. <-

And now, open your eyes and see what is written in the *Zohar* <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism, or Kabbalah</note> in the portion of *Vayeshev* <note>original: "p' Vayeshev"; the Torah portion beginning at Genesis 37:1</note>:
Rabbi Abba said: "And 'when you awake, she will talk with you' <note>Proverbs 6:22</note>. What is meant by 'she will talk with you'? It means that even though they now rise from the dust, the Torah <note>original: *Oraita*</note> will not be forgotten by them. For then they will know all that Torah which they left behind when they departed from this world. That Torah is preserved from that time, and it will enter into their inner being, and all things will be established more perfectly than they were at first. For all those words that he was not able to grasp properly—even though he strived for them but did not attain them—they all enter into his inner being and are rectified, and the Torah will speak within him. This is the meaning of: 'When you awake, she will talk with you.'"

He explained those matters that he was striving for during his lifetime but was unable to direct toward the truth <note>meaning he could not reach the full, hidden depth of the meaning</note>; when he rises for the <term>Resurrection: the *Techiyat HaMetim*, the belief that the dead will be restored to life in the future</term>, he will understand them in their root and essence.

And in the portion of *Vayishlach* <note>original: "p' Vayishlach"; the Torah portion beginning at Genesis 32:4</note>, Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> said: "All those words of Torah and all that Torah in which a person labored in this world—that Torah and those words stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and she <note>The Torah is personified here as a feminine entity</note> speaks before Him, and she raises her voice and is not silent. And at that time, she talks..."

...with his lips to make it heard to his ears. That which is settled upon his heart, he shall tell with the language of his pen, to benefit himself and others who heed his voice. This is because the enlightened person <note>term: *maskil* — a person of intellectual and spiritual understanding</note> who perceives within himself that he has attained some intellectual insight <note>term: *מושכל* (*moskal*) — a concept or truth grasped by the intellect</note> finds it impossible not to make it known to others, whether in writing or in speech. And I, the poor one who comes before Israel—a lowly foundation, a shepherd of ashes <note>original: "רוע' אפר" (*ro'eh efer*) — a biblical idiom from Isaiah 44:20 for one who pursues vanity or has a "deceived heart"</note>, whose heart has been misled—recognize my own lack of worth. My own thoughts argue back and forth within me. I was afraid, for I said to myself: "Perhaps I will record on my page that which will only reveal my own deficiency." I feared the hand of my pen’s faithfulness would testify to the shortness of my knowledge, and bring upon my inner being the blows of the critics and the arrows of the teachers toward my composition. 

Yet, my soul desired to know and understand words of insight. I found myself in the dilemma: "Woe to me if I speak, and woe to me if I do not speak" <note>A phrase from the Talmud (Tractate Bava Batra 89b) expressing the difficulty of choosing between two problematic options; here, the risk of speaking incorrectly versus the loss of withholding truth.</note>.

Regarding a similar situation, David, peace be upon him, said: "I was struck dumb with silence; I held my peace, even from good, and my sorrow was stirred. My heart was hot within me; while I was musing, the fire burned; then I spoke with my tongue" <note>Psalm 39:3-4</note>. He made known his pain and what he had intended in his heart: to guard himself from sinning with the expression of his tongue. He intended to be especially careful while the wicked were before him, lest they learn from his words to become heretics <note>term: *לפקר* (*lifkor*) — to abandon faith or act lawlessly</note>. But he realized that if he remained dumb with silence and did not speak—even as internal speech—he would remain in doubt and be silenced from the "good" he hoped for, and his pain would only be stirred. 

To escape both dilemmas, he agreed to speak with his tongue, saying: "O Lord, make me know my end," and so on, as is explained in the *Akedah* <note>The *Akedat Yitzchak*, a famous 15th-century philosophical and homiletic commentary by Rabbi Isaac Arama</note> in Gate 6. For this reason, if I ask properly, it is well; and if not, that...

...and his companions, and so on. Because the Scripture calls them "brothers," the Holy One desired to place His dwelling among them and never depart from them. Thus it is written: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together" <note>original: "שבת אחים גם יחד" (*shevet achim gam yachad*); Psalm 133:1</note>. 

And in the Torah portion *Bo* <note>The second book of Exodus</note>, come and see: the Holy One does not stand to watch over the deeds of any of the nations of the world, except for Israel alone. This is because these are the children of the Holy One, blessed be He. When the deeds of Israel are not found to be as they should be, then—as it were—those appointed messengers and emissaries who wish to testify regarding those deeds of Israel stand "over the Lord." This is the meaning of "to stand over the Lord" <note>original: "להתייצב על יי" (*le-hityatzev al Hashem*); a mystical interpretation of Zechariah 6:5 or Job 1:6, suggesting that human failings create a burden or "standing" against the Divine Presence</note>. For when Israel performs deeds that are not proper, they—as it were—weaken the strength of the Holy One, blessed be He. Through proper deeds.

And in the Torah portion *Vayikra* <note>The book of Leviticus</note>, it is said: "Let there be a firmament." These are Israel, who are the portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, and they take hold in that place called "Heaven" <note>term: *Shamayim* — Heaven</note>. This is the secret of the story where Rabbi Dosai the Elder once asked Rabbi Elai: "Behold, the Holy One gave the other nations great appointed ministers and rulers; but as for Israel, what place did He give them?" He replied to him: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven" <note>Genesis 1:17</note>. 

From all these teachings, we have learned that it is right and proper that there should be no power or any side-inclination of the celestial bodies <note>term: *mazal* — the influence of the stars or 'fate'</note> over the Chosen and Holy People. This holds true even when the deeds of men are mediocre and their fortune <note>mazal</note> is bad; even if one does not have enough merit in his hand to cancel the power of the bad fortune and cast its evil away from himself, he might live in sorrow and humiliation and be gathered [die] before his time. 

And regarding the union <note>term: *dibbuk* — here meaning a holy attachment or cleaving</note> that exists between us and the Omnipresent <note>term: *HaMakom* — 'The Place', a rabbinic name for God</note>, blessed be He, our Sages of blessed memory alluded to this in the saying: "You are called 'Man' (*Adam*), but the idolaters are not called 'Man'." The intention here is that the Name of the Lord <note>The Tetragrammaton (Y-H-V-H)</note> in its "filled" form <note>term: *gematria* — a system where Hebrew letters are assigned numerical values. 'Filling' a name means spelling out the names of the letters themselves</note>—*Yod*, *He*, *Vav*, *He*—reaches the numerical sum of "Adam" <note>The spelled-out letters YVD (20) + HA (6) + VV (12) + HA (6) equal 45, the same as the word ADM (Adam: 1+4+40). And one wonders: according to the degree that a man <note>original: "ב'נ" (*bar nash*); an Aramaic term for a human being or person</note> clings [to the Divine] and exerts himself in this world, so shall they arise in a complete state for eternal life, as we have said. This is especially puzzling since we have established the high stature of man at his creation; furthermore, all the worlds and the Torah are held and bound within them.

Go out and see what the *Zohar* wrote in the portion *Kedoshim* <note>the Book of Leviticus</note>: Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] opened and said, "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together" <note>Psalm 133:1</note>. Rather, Israel is attached to Him, and He is attached to them. Out of His love for them, the Holy One, blessed be He, first called us "servants," as it is written: "For to Me the children of Israel are servants; they are My servants" <note>Leviticus 25:55</note>. Ultimately, He called us "children," as it is written: "You are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. Later, He called us "brothers," as it is written: "For the sake of my brothers..." <note>Psalm 122:8</note>

And this [divine governance] is not only for unique individuals like Joshua—as it is written, "Sun, stand still at Gibeon" <note>Joshua 10:12; a reference to the biblical miracle where the sun stopped in its tracks for the Israelite leader</note> and similar cases—but rather it applies to the collective as a whole, without any other governing power ruling over them.

<meta>This page continues the argument from the previous discussion regarding the astrological influence on nations versus Israel's direct relationship with the Divine. It expands on the mystical definition of "Man" (Adam) and how the performance of the Shema prayer elevates the Jewish people above the celestial "system" (the Mazalot).</meta>

This is why you are called "Man" <note>original: "אדם" (*Adam*)</note>, meaning children of the Omnipresent <note>original: "למקום" (*la-Makom*), a Rabbinic title for God meaning "The Place," implying He encompasses the world</note> whose numerical value is "Man" <note>In the system of Gematria, the word *Adam* (אדם) totals 45, which is also the numerical value of one of the mystical expansions of the four-letter Name of God</note>. The nations of the world, however, are not called "Man" in this sense, for they are handed over to the celestial system <note>The "system" (*ma'arekhet*) refers to the predetermined laws of astrology and nature</note> as previously mentioned.

Regarding this topic, it is found in the Zohar, in the section of *Acharei Mot* <note>The Third Book of the Zohar, the foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>: That child opened his discourse and said, "'My people, what have I done to you? And how have I wearied you? Testify against me!'" <note>Micah 6:3</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "קב'ה" (*Kadosh Barukh Hu*)</note>, out of the love He has for Israel, called to them: "My people, what have I done? Why did I perform 'What' (*Mah*) for you?" He meant: "What have I required of you other than that you go to the synagogues and houses of study and testify of Me that I am One?"

This is as it is written: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One" <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note>. You must testify of Me that I am One and that I am exalted above the Name of forty-two letters <note>A powerful mystical Name of God composed of 42 letters, associated with the work of creation</note> which is found in the section of the Reading of the *Shema* <note>The central prayer of Jewish liturgy</note>, specifically the words from "And you shall love" until "And it shall come to pass if you obey." You shall make Me One over them.

The explanation of "What (*Mah*) have I done to you" relates to the numerical value of *Mah* (45), which is the Name mentioned in the scripture: "Let us make Man (*Adam*) in our image" <note>Genesis 1:26; *Mah* and *Adam* both equal 45, linking the human soul to a specific divine aspect</note>. But the nations of the world are not called "Man" plainly, but rather a "branch" of Man, as we find in the Zohar, section *Yitro*: "Come and see: it is written of Ishmael, 'And he shall be a wild-ass of a man' <note>Genesis 16:12</note>, but not 'Man' alone. Because he was circumcised, he entered the beginning stage of 'Man.'" The word for "wild-ass" (*pere*) is interpreted as a "branch" <note>The author connects the word *pere* to *purah*, a branch or bough</note>, like the verse "lopping off the boughs."

"And how have I wearied you?" For this alone did I "weary" you: by having you go every day to read the *Shema* to unify My Name—"The Lord our God, the Lord"—over the forty-two words in that section. With the addition of the three words "The Lord our God, the Lord," the total reaches forty-five <note>42 + 3 = 45, the value of *Mah* and *Adam*</note>. Therefore, the verse says "Testify against Me"—testify every day that I am One and unique over the forty-two, which is a hint to the Name of forty-two.

From all these aforementioned statements, the love of the Lord (may He be blessed) for His people who cleave to Him becomes clear, as does the connection and cleaving to the Lord and His Torah. It is therefore proper and right that the entire system of the heavens, their constellations, and their domains be surrendered and obedient to all who are called by the name of Israel.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into the nature of the human soul and its relationship with the Divine. <page-type>text</page-type>
<sig>c ij</sig>

...it escapes, whether this soul is merely a power and a potentiality <note>original: "כח וההכנה" (*koach ve-hakhana*), terms from Aristotelian philosophy describing the soul as a function of the body rather than an independent entity</note> existing within the formations of the body and renewed as the body is renewed, or whether it is a separate essence <term>separate essence: a spiritual substance that exists independently of physical matter</term> standing on its own, which only has the bond of existence joined to it during its physical formation, etc.

Until finally, he posed the question, saying: "If we assume this essence is separate in itself, yet it is found to be as lowly as matter <note>original: "וזל' חמר" (*ve-zal chomer*), implying the soul becomes cheapened or degraded by its association with the physical</note>, how did the wisdom of its Creator decree to place it under the stumbling hand of this companionship? Why pair it with this loathsome and filthy matter, which always turns toward every act of transgression? It is from this matter that evil is first opened unto the soul; for the matter, He prepared the instruments of death and absolute destruction. Through this companionship, the soul is at risk of falling into the lowest of pits, regarding which the punishment was testified by Him, may He be exalted: 'And I will destroy that soul' <note>Leviticus 23:30</note>, and 'that soul shall utterly be cut off; its iniquity shall be upon it' <note>Numbers 15:31; this refers to *Karet*, a spiritual excision from the source of life</note>."

And it says: "But the souls of your enemies, He shall sling them out as from the hollow of a sling" <note>1 Samuel 25:29</note>. And it is said: "And you shall trample the wicked" <note>Malachi 3:21/4:3</note>. Furthermore, our Sages of blessed memory said: "These are the transgressors of Israel who sin with their bodies; their bodies perish and their souls are burned" <note>Talmud, Rosh Hashanah 17a. This passage discusses the ultimate fate of those who abandon the path of the soul for the desires of the flesh</note>.

Would it not have been better for the soul to remain in its initial divine dwelling, in tranquility and quiet, rather than to disguise itself and enter the thick of battle? <note>The "battlefield" is a common metaphor for physical life, where the soul must fight against the inclinations of the body</note>. For almost all who enter that battle do not return unscathed. As the general saying goes: "It would have been more comfortable for man had he not been created than to have been created" <note>Talmud, Eruvin 13b; a famous conclusion of the Schools of Hillel and Shammai regarding the difficulty of maintaining spiritual purity in the physical world</note>.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical inquiry into the soul's nature, specifically addressing the transition from a physical life force to an eternal, spiritual intellect. It builds on the previous page's question of why a pure soul is joined to a material body by proposing that the soul evolves through distinct stages of development.</meta>

The souls that remain after death are not the same soul that exists at the time of a person's formation. For that which exists when a person is first formed is merely the **power of preparation** <term>Koach ha-Hakhanah: A philosophical term for potentiality—the capacity of a physical body to eventually host a higher intellect.</term> alone. However, the "separate thing" that remains after death is that which has been established in **actuality** <note>original: *be-po’al*. In medieval philosophy, something "in actuality" has moved from being a mere potential to a realized, existing truth.</note>, and so on.

He explained that the **vital soul** <term>Nefesh: The lowest level of the soul, associated with biological life and basic human nature.</term> is what is found within a person at the beginning of his existence, while he is in his first state of development. Afterward, as he progresses through his short life and opens his eyes further to the ways of the Torah and the Commandments, his **intellect** <note>original: *sekhel*</note> prevails, and the **spirit** <term>Ruach: The middle level of the soul, representing the moral and emotional growth achieved through action and study.</term> comes to rest upon him. This occurs because that original essence has already substantialized itself to become a separate spiritual entity.

When a person adds even greater strength to this—by habituating himself to this level with the ultimate zeal and a longing to ascend and "see the face of the Lord his God"—the **highest soul** <term>Neshama: The most refined level of the soul, representing the perfected human intellect in communion with the Divine.</term> enters him, which is the most perfect of all levels.

This general principle emerges from his words, though he elaborated at great length in his explanation. It is clarified through his words that the doubts arising concerning the essence of the soul (which he previously mentioned) forced him to explain that the souls which remain [after death] are not the same soul that exists at the moment of formation.

However, when we search, searching again and again, a resolution for all these doubts will be found; and your sign <note>A "sign" or *siman* is a mnemonic device or scriptural hint used to remember a concept.</note> for this is: "And he searched..." <note>A reference to Genesis 44:12, used here to emphasize the necessity of deep investigation to find the truth.</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the relationship between the soul and the physical body. Having established that the soul is a spiritual entity that descends into a material "vessel," the text now explains how this union allows a human being to bridge the gap between the divine heavens and the earthly world.</meta>

...the **Small World** <term>Olam ha-Katan: The Microcosm; the philosophical concept that the human body is a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</term>. Likewise, the **soul** <note>original: *Neshama*</note> is a likeness of the **Great World** <term>Olam ha-Gadol: The Macrocosm; the vast universe or the divine structure of reality.</term>. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Just as the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu*—the standard Hebrew title for God.</note> sees but is not seen, and just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, sustains the entire world, so too does the soul" and so forth.

Since the body is the likeness of the Small World and the soul is the likeness of the Great World, then when the soul clothes itself within the body, a human being is found to be a likeness of both the **upper and lower realms** <note>original: *elyonim ve-tachtonim*; the spiritual and physical dimensions of creation.</note>.

The benefit of the soul entering into this body is to manifest its powers and actions in this world, for it requires its "vessels" <note>original: *keleiha*. This refers to the physical limbs and organs that serve as tools for the soul's expression in the physical realm.</note> as we have previously stated. Upon its descent to this world, the soul adds power and **divine abundance** <term>Shefa: A mystical term for the flow of energy or grace from God that sustains and directs existence.</term> to lead this lowly world. It is then perfected through a rectification of both "above and below," allowing its vitality to reach a higher state, integrated from all sides.

If it were not comprised of both what is above and what is below, it would not be **complete** <term>Sheleimah: Characterized by spiritual wholeness, integrity, or perfection.</term>. Thus, we find that before the soul descends to this world, it belongs to the mystery of the upper realm; but when it is within the body, it is completed and encompasses this lower world as well. 

Therefore, when the soul eventually departs from this world, it is perfected with the completeness of both worlds—above and below—provided that the person lived in **awe of his Creator** <note>original: *yere le-kono*</note> and unified a complete soul through the power of goodness.

<meta>This page continues the investigation into why the divine soul must leave its heavenly origin. # Concerning the resolution of the doubt as to why the soul descends
# into the world, according to the **Zohar** <term>Zohar: Literally "The Splendor," the foundational work of Kabbalah (Jewish mysticism), traditionally attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</term>.

It is like a king who had a son born to him. He sent the boy to a village to be raised and brought up until he had matured, so that they might teach him the conduct and customs of the king’s palace. The king eventually heard that his son had matured and grown; what did he do? Out of love for his son, he sent the **Matronita** <term>Matronita: A term used in the Zohar for the Queen, representing the Shekhinah—the feminine, indwelling presence of God that mediates between the divine and the physical world.</term>, his mother, to bring him back, and he brought him into his palace and rejoiced with him every day. 

In this same way, the **Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: *Kadosh Barukh Hu*, a standard Hebrew title for God.</note> sired a son through the **Matronita**, and who is this? It is the high, holy **soul** <term>Neshama: The highest level of the human soul, representing the divine spark and intellect.</term>. Regarding the three [levels]: **Nefesh**, **Ruach**, and **Neshamah**. <term>Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah: These are the three primary levels of the soul in Jewish mysticism. Nefesh (the vital/animal soul) is the lowest, Ruach (the spirit/emotional soul) is the middle, and Neshamah (the intellectual/divine soul) is the highest.</term> All of them are included one within the other, and their power is found in three distinct places.

**Nefesh**: This is found within the grave when the body is worn away in the earth. Through this [part of the soul], it wanders in this world to be found among the living, to know of their pain, and in the hour when they are in need, it requests mercy for them. <note>original: *be-at rachamei*; This reflects the traditional belief that the lowest part of the soul remains near the physical remains to intercede for the living.</note>

**Neshamah**: This ascends immediately to its place—to that place from which it emerged—and so on.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and mystical exploration of the soul's nature. And through the desire to ascend and to behold the face of the Lord <note>original: *יי* — the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God.</note> our God, the **Neshamah** <term>Neshamah: the highest of the three levels of the soul, representing the breath of God and the seat of the intellect</term> enters into him, which is the most complete of the soul's levels.

This is also the opinion of the **Author of the Akedah** <note>Isaac Arama (c. 1420–1494), a Spanish rabbi and philosopher famous for his work *Akedat Yitzchak* (The Binding of Isaac), which blended philosophy with homiletics.</note>. Regarding this level of soul, the Sages said: "it is better for him to have been created," because it is a potentiality that moves from one elevation to another. Indeed, every form of existence is better than its absence.

However, for those Sages who argued that "it is better for him *not* to have been created" <note>This refers to a famous debate in the Talmud (Tractate Eruvin 13b) between the School of Hillel and the School of Shammai about whether the struggle of human life makes existence worth the risk of sin.</note>, they hold the view that the soul is a **separate substance** from the very beginning of man’s existence. Therefore, they said it would be better not to have been created, for there are many who bring death upon their own souls by following after their physical desires and after "imaginary acquisitions" <note>Worldly wealth and status that have no permanence in the afterlife.</note>.

Regarding this, some of our Sages of blessed memory have written that the **commandments** do not add a new power of perfection to the soul's own essence. Rather, because the soul has fallen into a "turbid valley" <note>The physical world, viewed here as a lowly or murky place for a celestial soul.</note>, the **practical commandments** <term>practical commandments: *Mitzvot Ma’asiyot*, the physical actions and rituals required by Jewish law</term> were given. I refer here to the warnings against forbidden unions, forbidden foods, ritual impurity, and the like. These were given so that **matter** <gloss>the physical body</gloss> would not become utterly detestable; instead, the body should remain refined and always prepared to sustain the soul rather than destroying it. There are also commandments intended to constantly remind the soul of the Lord, so that it may always stand firm in spiritual matters...

This is what they called the **acquired intellect** <term>acquired intellect: *Sekhel ha-Nikneh*, the state where the human intellect has successfully realized its potential by connecting with divine wisdom</term>. ### 17

The matter of the soul <note>original: *Neshamah*, referring to the highest level of the human soul</note> being a noble substance and created beforehand, yet not being found within the body upon its entry into the world's atmosphere, shall be explained in a 
->vigorous<- 
manner.

---

And if so, what benefit is found for the soul by being present in the body upon its entry into the world? Are not all its faculties resting and dormant in the womb, and so on? Furthermore, the Torah and the commandments <note>original: *mitzvot*</note> are meant to be performed through active deeds <note>original: *kum v’aseh*, a legal term for positive commandments requiring action.</note>. It is not at all a strange thing to wonder at; likewise, a person does not contemplate with the <term>intellectual soul</term> <note>original: *nefesh ha-maskelet*, the faculty of reason and higher understanding</note>—whose dwelling place is in the brain—during the time of their infancy and childhood, because those faculties are of no use to them then. This was elaborated upon by the author of the <term>Duties of the Hearts</term> <note>original: *Chovot HaLevavot*, a classic work of Jewish ethics and philosophy by Bahya ibn Paquda</note> in the "Gate of Reflection" <note>original: *Sha'ar HaBechinah*</note>.

Similarly, the scripture states, “[He] gives a soul to the people upon it” (Isaiah 42:5). It does not say “to the newborns upon it,” but “to the people upon it.” This means it is given to a "people" who are fit for <term>divine service</term> <note>original: *Avodat HaShem*</note>, just as it is written: “Let My people go, that they may serve Me” (Exodus 8:1). It does not refer to the time of birth, when one is not yet fit for divine service. Rather, [it refers to] when the time arrives that he knows and understands in his mind how to reject the evil and [choose the good...]

<summary>The author argues that the noble "intellectual soul" remains dormant during infancy because the child is not yet capable of divine service or active performance of commandments. He supports this using the philosophy of Bahya ibn Paquda and a specific reading of Isaiah 42:5.</summary>

# The words of the **Ba'al Akeidah** <note>original: *Ba'al Akeidah*, referring to Rabbi Isaac Arama (c. 1420–1494), a Spanish Jewish philosopher and communal leader known for his work "Akeidat Yitzchak"</note> who explained the verse:

---

The aforementioned teacher of blessed memory reads in the **Sifra of the House of Rav** <note>An ancient legal commentary on the book of Leviticus</note> regarding what is written in the Torah portion of *Vayishlach* <note>The section of Genesis covering Jacob's return and his wrestling with the angel</note>, as follows: "And I have heard from many that there is a passage in the **Midrash HaNe'elam** <note>original: *Midrash Ha-Ne'elam*, 'The Hidden Midrash,' which is a specific layer of the Zohar that blends philosophy and mysticism</note> that states: 'Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sciatic nerve'—the word *et* <note>A Hebrew grammatical particle that often implies something additional</note> serves to include the fast of **Tisha B'Av** <note>The ninth day of the month of Av, the primary day of mourning and fasting commemorating the destruction of the Holy Temples in Jerusalem</note>." 

Many were puzzled by this statement because its reason was not known <insert>▬</insert> to them. I was asked about it and was stunned for a time. Then, a fitting explanation occurred to me, and I said: "If this passage truly exists in reality, it is quite clear." This is its interpretation:

Within this verse are hinted the **four fasts** <note>The four traditional days of fasting that mourn the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple: the 17th of Tammuz, the 9th of Av, the 3rd of Tishrei, and the 10th of Tevet</note> of the year, which were brought upon us as a result of the "striking of the hip socket" <note>Jacob’s injury, which mystically represents the historical vulnerabilities and persecutions of his descendants, the Jewish people</note>. 

The word *ha-nasheh* <note>meaning 'the displaced' or 'the forgotten'</note> acts as an anagram for *ha-shanah* <note>'the year'</note>. This implies: "Therefore the children of Israel do not eat [fast] throughout the year..."

If the matter were so, it would be impossible for any person to acquire that **perfection** <note>original: *ha-shleimut*. Rather, the understanding of the matter is that a single **commandment** <term>original: *mitzvah*. For if all of them were absolutely necessary to acquire perfection, this would not be a "merit" but rather a heavy "obligation."

The ideal state of performing a divine service purely for the love of God, rather than for recognition or reward.</term>...

# Open Your Eyes! What Is Found in the Zohar, Portion of "Shelach"
## Go To the Greatness of Righteous Women in the World of Souls

**Rabbi Shimon** <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is traditionally attributed.</note> said to **Elijah** <note>The prophet Elijah, who in mystical literature often appears to reveal heavenly secrets to the sages.</note>: "I have one matter I wish to know. If you are able to inform me regarding the **women in that world** <note>original: *nashin be-hahu alma*. This refers to the afterlife or the world of souls.</note>—whether they merit to ascend on high, or how they are situated there."

Elijah replied: "Rabbi, Rabbi! In this matter we have special permission, provided we do not reveal all the **secrets** <term>original: *sitrin*. Hidden mystical truths that are usually kept from the uninitiated.</term> that are there. Six **palaces** <term>original: *heichalin*. In Kabbalah, these are spiritual chambers or levels of heaven through which souls ascend.</term> appeared to me, filled with many delights and pleasures, and a veil is spread in the **Garden of Eden** <note>original: *Ginnata de-Eden*. The paradise where righteous souls enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence.</note>. From that veil onward, males do not enter at all.

In one palace resides **Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh** <note>The Egyptian princess who rescued Moses from the Nile. In Jewish tradition, she is considered a righteous woman who earned a place in Paradise while still alive.</note>, and many tens of thousands and thousands of righteous women are with her. Every single one of them has places of light and delights, without any crowding at all. Three times every day, a herald proclaims: 'Behold, the image of **Moses, the faithful prophet** <note>original: *Moshe nevia meheimna*. A standard title for Moses in the Zohar, emphasizing his unique reliability as a conduit for God's word.</note>, is coming!' 

Then Bithiah goes out to a certain place where there is a curtain, and she sees the image of Moses and bows before him. She says: 'Blessed is my portion, for I raised this light!' This is her delight, more than all others. She then returns to the women, and they all occupy themselves with the **commandments of the Torah** <term>original: *pikudei oraita*. The 613 laws or religious duties found in the Five Books of Moses.</term> in those forms."

<meta>This page provides the cosmological and anthropological framework for the distinction between souls discussed on the previous page. It explains how the human soul is structured to mirror the three levels of the universe—the Angelic, the Spherical, and the Terrestrial—plus a fourth, Divine level that was lost by most of humanity after the Tower of Babel.</meta>

**He, may He be blessed** <note>original: *Yit'*, an abbreviation for *Yitbarekh*</note>, created the world divided into three. First, the **Angelic World** <term>Angelic World: *Ha-Olam ha-Malakhi*. In medieval cosmology, this is the highest created realm, consisting of pure, non-physical intellects.</term>, which is characterized by absolute simplicity. After it is the [unclear] **Spherical World** <term>Spherical World: *Ha-Olam ha-Galgali*. The realm of the celestial spheres (planets and stars), believed to be made of a "pure matter" that is eternal and unchanging.</term>, which is material, yet made of pure and clean matter, beautiful and eternal. And after it is the **Lower World** <term>Lower World: *Ha-Olam ha-Shefel*. Our terrestrial world, composed of the four elements and characterized by the cycle of birth and death.</term>, which is material, turbid, subject to existence [unclear] and destruction.

He intended to create a pattern from these three creations of His, and from Himself, **may He be blessed** <note>original: *Yit'*</note>, their Creator. He consulted with them to say, "Let us make man in our **image and after our likeness**" <note>Genesis 1:26</note>, for the matter of **image and likeness** <term>Image and Likeness: *Tzelem u-Demut*. Here interpreted philosophically as the "form" or essential nature that defines what a being is.</term> is the form by which a being is what it is. 

And therefore, in the **First Man** <note>Adam</note>, there were found four souls—meaning four powers within the soul. Namely: 
1. The **vegetative soul** <term>Vegetative soul: *Nefesh ha-Tzomekhat*. The faculty responsible for biological growth and nutrition.</term>, whose dwelling is in the liver, which is the image of the **Lower World**. 
2. The **sensory soul** <term>Sensory soul: *Nefesh ha-Margeshet*. The faculty of perception, feeling, and movement.</term>, whose dwelling is in the heart, which is the image of the **Spherical World**. 
3. The **intellectual soul** <term>Intellectual soul: *Nefesh ha-Maskelet*. The faculty of reason and logic.</term>, whose dwelling is in the brain of the head, which is the image of the **Angelic World**. 
4. And a **Divine soul** <term>Divine soul: *Nefesh Elohit*. A direct spark of the Divine essence that transcends the created celestial hierarchies.</term>, which has no specific dwelling, just as there is no specific dwelling for God, **may He be blessed** <note>original: *El Yit'*</note>, who is the "image" of the World; for He dwells in the heavens and "the whole earth is full of His glory" <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. 

The standing of these four souls continued in the descendants of Adam [unclear] until the **Generation of the Division** <term>Generation of the Division: *Dor ha-Pelagah*. The generation of the Tower of Babel, when humanity was dispersed and their languages confounded.</term>. At that time, the Lord separated [unclear] them from His presence and removed from them His image, the **Image of God** [unclear]. In its place, only the **Angelic image** remained for them. And it [the Divine soul/image] was then placed in **Abraham**...

<summary>The author describes the human soul as a microcosm reflecting three cosmic levels (Angelic, Spherical, and Terrestrial) plus a Divine level. # Speaking on the Resolution of the Doubt Left Above
## According to the Zohar.

In the Book of the Zohar <note>The primary work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah), attributed to the circle of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</note>, in the portion of *Vayeishev* <note>The section of the Torah beginning at Genesis 37:1.</note>, these are the words: 

"There are five times when the **moon** <note>original: *sihara*. In Kabbalah, the moon represents the *Shekhinah* (Divine Presence) which receives and reflects divine light.</note> is in a state of deficiency and dwells in **judgment** <term>Judgment: *Dina*. A divine state characterized by strict law, limitation, and rigor, as opposed to Mercy.</term>. During these times, the **sun** <note>original: *shimsha*. The sun represents the masculine principle of Mercy (*Chesed*) that balances the Moon.</note> is not found with it. 

Yet, at every time and every hour, the moon must bring forth **souls** <note>original: *nishmatin*</note> into human beings—just as it gathered them at first, it brings them out now. At the time when the moon stands in judgment, whoever receives their soul at this moment will always exist in deficiency, and **poverty** follows them. Such a person is constantly broken by judgment all the days of their life, whether they are **guilty** or **righteous**. 

The exception is that **prayer** <note>original: *tzaluta*</note> cancels all decrees of judgment, and one is able to ascend through prayer to that time when that spiritual degree stands in perfection. Then, that **river that flows and emerges** <term>The Flowing River: *Nahara de-nagid ve-nafik*. A technical term for the stream of divine emanation that provides sustenance to all worlds.</term> is utilized. Then, the soul that emerges and cleaves to that human being allows that person to be perfected in everything: in wealth, in children, and in the health of the body. And all of this is because of that **luck** <note>original: *mazala*. While often translated as 'luck,' it refers to the 'dripping' of influence from the higher celestial spheres.</note> that flows."

<summary>The author uses a passage from the Zohar to explain that a person's worldly fortune is determined by the spiritual state of the "Moon" (the Shekhinah) at the moment their soul descends, though prayer remains a powerful tool to override this celestial decree.</summary>
